# Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) — facts

> Source-anchored units about Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy): 18 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · 18 units · 4 sources · rights: quote -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] An API key consists of a Public Key and Private Key used for HTTP Digest authentication. MongoDB’s curl example uses --user with the pair and --digest. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md

## How it works

- [statement] The organization IP-access-list requirement is conditional: UI-created organizations require it by default, but disabling the requirement permits Internet requests when the list is empty. A populated list restricts originating addresses. Missing entries under the requirement can cause HTTP 403. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy)
- [statement] HashiCorp’s Atlas secrets engine generates a Programmatic API Key per Vault lease and automatically revokes it when the lease expires unless renewed. This expiry is managed by Vault; it is not evidence that ordinary Atlas API keys have the same built-in TTL. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/mongodbatlas — https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/mongodbatlas · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy)
- [statement] Vault’s MongoDB Atlas secrets engine creates programmatic API keys per lease with organization or project roles and optional IP restrictions. Vault revokes these credentials when their leases expire unless renewed; this is Vault-managed lifetime behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/mongodbatlas — https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/mongodbatlas · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy)

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A 2021 Terraform provider 0.7.0 issue records a final Unauthorized error during import even though curl with the same key succeeded after an initial HTTP 401 Digest challenge and subsequent HTTP 200. Inspect the completed authentication exchange before treating every 401 line as proof of unusable credentials. This is historical evidence, not a verified current provider defect. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/issues/385 · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The Atlas creation workflow displays the private key only once and instructs users to save it securely. Microsoft stores discovery secrets in VS Code Secret Storage and warns against placing credentials in source control. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md ; https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-credentials.html — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-credentials

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB documents API keys as a supported legacy Atlas Administration API authentication method and recommends service accounts instead; legacy status alone does not establish a removal date. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/auth/authentication.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access-org.md
- [statement] API keys authorize Atlas Administration API operations, not UI access or direct reads or writes of cluster data. Database connections require separate database-user credentials; Microsoft's DocumentDB extension for Visual Studio Code documents the same separation for Atlas resource discovery. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas ; https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-credentials — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-credentials
- [statement] Each API-key pair belongs to one organization and may receive access to any number of projects within it. Microsoft's DocumentDB extension for Visual Studio Code (its MongoDB Atlas service discovery) requires a separate credential for each additional organization. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-credentials
- [statement] Assigned organization and project roles constrain what a key can do. HashiCorp’s Atlas secrets engine likewise issues keys with designated roles and can configure their allowed IP addresses or CIDR ranges. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/mongodbatlas — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/mongodbatlas
- [statement] MongoDB displays the Private Key only once during creation, so automation owners must securely save it at that point. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy)
- [statement] HashiCorp maintains a separate Atlas secrets-engine plugin for generating ephemeral Programmatic API Keys; this provides a concrete implementation lead for key lifecycle automation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/mongodbatlas — https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/mongodbatlas · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-mongodbatlas
- [statement] The Atlas API authentication documentation establishes that API keys belong to one organization and that roles limit their operations. The API access setup documentation describes an optional IP access list for the Atlas Administration API. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md
- [statement] MongoDB labels API keys legacy and recommends service accounts; current Terraform documentation still supports programmatic keys alongside its recommended service-account method. Legacy does not establish that keys have been removed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/index.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/guides/provider-configuration.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/blob/master/docs/guides/provider-configuration.md
- [statement] Each API-key pair belongs to one organization. Project visibility and permitted operations depend on assigned access and roles; Microsoft instructs users to configure credentials for each organization they need to browse. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md ; https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-credentials
- [statement] Vault’s Atlas API-key secrets engine and its Atlas database plugin issue different credentials: the former generates programmatic API keys, while the latter generates ephemeral database-user credentials and uses Atlas API keys for its management integration. (high confidence) Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/mongodbatlas ; https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/mongodbatlas — https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/secret/mongodbatlas · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy) · also: https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-mongodbatlas
- [statement] The Atlas Terraform provider accepts public_key/private_key credentials, including MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_API_KEY and MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_API_KEY environment variables. Its migration guidance replaces these with service-account credentials and validates the change with terraform plan. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/blob/master/docs/guides/provider-configuration.md · keywords: Atlas Programmatic API Keys (Legacy)
- [statement] HashiCorp's Atlas database-plugin acceptance-test instructions say a free tier cluster can be provisioned manually for testing and require Atlas API public and private keys. This scopes the evidence to that workflow, not every Administration API operation.
